stemMd: Why did some passengers leave home well before the average journey time required?

options.label: A
options.textMd: They were paid for arriving early.

options.label: B
options.textMd: The second route had no timetable at all.

options.label: C
options.textMd: They preferred the longest possible journey.

options.label: D
options.textMd: They wanted to reduce the risk of arriving late.

options.label: E
options.textMd: The two routes had different average journey times.

explanationMd: The passage explicitly says lateness had a greater cost than early arrival. Passengers therefore allowed extra time for unpredictable delays. This is a response to variability even when average time looks acceptable.

distractorRationale.c: Their behaviour responds to the cost of lateness.
distractorRationale.b: The passage does not say this.
distractorRationale.e: The first sentence says the averages were the same.
